transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi… yeah. I came in because I’m kind of overwhelmed trying to keep my schoolwork and my little accessories shop organized at the same time. Like, I’ll have assignment notes somewhere, due dates in another place, receipts shoved in a drawer, and supplies just… in piles. 

And then I’ll try to start fixing it, but I end up moving things around instead of actually knowing what to do first. It’s frustrating because the shop is small, it’s not like some huge business or anything, but somehow the beads and packaging and papers make it feel huge. And then school stuff gets mixed in with it, and I just feel stuck.
Do you have similar problems with staying organized and starting tasks in other areas of your life, or does this mainly happen with your schoolwork and the shop?

It’s mostly the schoolwork and the shop, I think… because that’s where all the stuff is. Like the due dates and assignment notes and then the receipts and little bags and beads, and I’ll put them “just for now” somewhere, and then it’s a pile.

But I guess it kind of blends into everything because I’ll be trying to clean it up and then I find something random, like a charm I forgot I bought, and suddenly I’m thinking about making a whole new set instead of figuring out what assignment is due first. So yeah, the big problem is getting those two organized at the same time and knowing where to even start.

Outside of your schoolwork and the shop, do you find yourself struggling to stay focused or organized — for example, with daily routines like chores, planning your day, or keeping track of personal items?

Yeah, I mean… I’m not sure it’s as bad with like, normal daily stuff, but it kind of turns into the same thing when school and the shop are involved. Like my room becomes the place where everything lands — assignment notes, due dates I wrote down on random paper, receipts, little bags, beads, supplies — and then I’m like, okay, I need to organize this, but I don’t know what to do first.

And then I’ll start with one pile, but it reminds me of another pile, and then I’m looking at packaging ideas instead of finding my homework notes. So… outside of that, I guess it spills over because those things are everywhere, but the main thing is I can’t get the schoolwork and my little shop organized at the same time.
Do you find that these difficulties with staying on task and getting organized affect other parts of your life, like relationships, sleep, or your performance in school?

Yeah… it has. I mean, school especially. I missed some required steps for my program because I didn’t keep track of what was supposed to be done, and now my financial aid is kind of at risk, which is really scary.

And with the shop stuff, it’s not just me being messy anymore. People I’ve worked with on little projects, like custom sets or helping with packaging ideas, they don’t really depend on me as much now. Which… I get it, because I’ll say I’m going to handle something and then I lose track of the steps. But it still feels bad.

Do you find it hard to stay focused or follow through on tasks even when they aren’t related to school or your shop, like listening during conversations, finishing chores, or reading something from start to finish?

Yeah… I think so. Like, even if it’s not exactly the shop or school, I’ll be listening to something and I start out fine, like I’m really trying to pay attention, and then a few minutes later my brain is somewhere else.

Like in class, or if I’m watching a video for one of my business assignments, I’ll suddenly be thinking about charm designs or, oh, maybe this would be a cute order idea, and then I realize I missed half of what they said. And then I have to rewind it, but sometimes I get distracted again while rewinding, which is… annoying. So yeah, staying with something from beginning to end is hard sometimes.
When did you first start having trouble staying focused or getting organized? Was this something you noticed in school earlier, like when you were younger, or did it seem to come on more recently?

I think it was earlier, honestly. Like, not just recent. My mom actually still has some of my elementary school notes, which is kind of embarrassing because she keeps everything in these folders — like old report cards, random art projects, even this weird paper turkey thing I made — but yeah, there were notes from teachers saying I was always getting out of my seat, talking before I got called on, and rushing through group activities.

And the thing is, I usually understood the work, so it wasn’t like I couldn’t do it. I’d just… move too fast or jump in before I was supposed to. So I guess it goes back to when I was little, not just now.
